newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat up on freeze damage data, commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat up on freeze damage data, commercials.

text.p: Data from ongoing tours this week of U.S. hard red winter wheat areas and commercial buying helped push CBOT prices higher at midsession, CBOT floor traders said.
"Regarding the tours, we're beginning to see more confirmation of frost damage because they're into the areas that were hit," said one wheat trader.

Both the Wheat Quality Council's tour of Kansas and another wheat tour moving through Oklahoma were reporting increased incidence of frost damage Wednesday following reports of favorable conditions on Tuesday.
The Oklahoma tour pegged that state's crop at 109.9 million bushels, down from an earlier Oklahoma State University forecast of 121.34 million.

Commercials were also noted buyers in the wheat pit, traders said. In early trade, ADM bought 500,000 bushels July, and Cargill, Inc. and Continental Grain each bought one million July, pit sources said.
LIT America and Smith Barney were sellers, selling one million bushels of July each, traders said.
At 1112 CDT, CBOT wheat was down three cents per bushel to up seven cents, with July six cents higher at $4.08-1/2.
